claim: estimate.temporal_response.gcomp internal known-truth conformance for a pulse dose by horizon surface

surface.band_note: Bands are not in this section: the pre-1.9 analytic delta-method band treated lag-aligned rows as independent and was retired; the seeded circular-block bands are pinned under block_band.

block_band.note: Determinism pin of the seeded circular-block bootstrap through the public Study API (ExecutionContext seed 21, 60 replicates, serial and bounded-thread contexts agree bit for bit). Not a coverage claim: coverage evidence is the weekly gate crates/antecedent/tests/v19_temporal_response_calibration.rs. The noiseless period-4 DGP makes every estimating score degenerate or negatively dependent, so testing lengthens nothing and the block stays at the rule (16). That length is a multiple of the period: every circular resample stays orthogonal and the band collapses to the point surface (GEMM-scale width). The old |dose|-scaled analytic band vanished only at dose zero; these cells collapse together.

support.note: Period-4 T in {-1,0,1} so the union of horizon ranges equals the intersection; both requested doses sit inside every lag-aligned window. Mixed-horizon support is pinned on conformance/response/temporal_horizon_support.

sustained_effect_projection.note: Licensed SustainedEffect is the single-step window (from == until) at treatment_offset; multi-step Sustained remains estimator-refused.

estimator_contract.estimator: temporal response linear g-computation over horizon-specific lag-aligned OLS designs
estimator_contract.claim: the deterministic finite sample makes the omitted treatment lag orthogonal to each fitted treatment column, so the estimator recovers the analytic structural surface
estimator_contract.not_claimed: no external-package parity or recursive simulation; multiplicative and truncated Soft remain refused; nested Sequence remains refused

tolerance.band_note: block_band values are compared at relative tolerance band_rtol; surface.mean and the intervention paths at atol

generation.outcome_sequence: y_i = 1 + 2*t_(i-1) + 3*t_(i-2), with pre-sample treatment values equal to 0
generation.note: For n=242, both lag-aligned OLS windows have zero-mean adjacent treatment columns and zero adjacent cross-product; intercepts and lag coefficients are exactly (1,2) and (1,3).
